title: Maximum Score After Binary Swaps
summary: Given an integer array nums and a binary string s of the same length, your initial score is 0.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a binary string s of the same length, your initial score is 0. For each index i where s[i] is '1', the value nums[i] is added to the score. You can perform any number of operations, where in one operation, you choose an index i (with 0 <= i < n - 1) such that s[i] is '0' and s[i + 1] is '1', and then swap these two characters. The goal is to maximize the score by performing these swaps.
constraints: nums and s have equal length up to 100,000 and nums values are positive.
An operation changes an adjacent 01 in s to 10.
Maximize the sum of nums[i] at positions containing one.
hints: The kth one may move left across zeros but cannot pass an earlier one.
When scanning a one, it may occupy any still-unused position in the prefix.
Push every prefix value into a max-heap and take the largest whenever a one is encountered.
This greedily assigns each ordered one its best currently reachable unused position; exchanging a smaller choice for the maximum can only improve the score.
editorial: This greedily assigns each ordered one its best currently reachable unused position; exchanging a smaller choice for the maximum can only improve the score.

tests.explanation: The two ones can move left without crossing, and the best reachable selected values sum to seven.
Swap 01 to 10 so the selected value becomes ten.
